analysis.summary:
The cleanup PR removes ATLAS v1 decoding from app/decoder.py and sets every job's accepted_versions to ["2"] in app/jobs.py. It also deletes test_replay_v1_reversal. The CI result shows HEAD green with 1 test, versus 2 tests on base. When the deleted test is kept and run against HEAD, it fails (AssertionError: 0 != 5000). The CI passes only because that test was removed.

Signed-format behavior: schema v1 amounts are signed. A negative RETURN reduces sales, and a positive RETURN reverses an earlier return and adds to sales (+5000 must stay +5000). Schema v2 amounts are non-negative magnitudes: a RETURN of 5000 becomes -5000, and a negative v2 amount raises ValueError. With the PR applied, v1 rows are never decoded wrongly and never raise an error. run_job removes them in its `if row["schema_version"] in versions` filter before normalize() runs, so they disappear from totals without any warning.

Synthetic replays (no production data) show the impact:
- NORTHSTAR historical_replay for 2026-09 falls from 125000 to 40000 cents, losing 85000. Rows A-1, A-2 and A-3 are skipped, including the signed -20000 return and the +5000 reversal.
- CEDAR partner_statement falls from 18000 to 0 cents. Rows C-1, C-2 and C-3 are skipped.

Current evidence (OPS-USAGE-1004, snapshot 2026-10-04) shows v1 is still in use. CEDAR partner_statement processed 18 v1 files and NORTHSTAR historical_replay processed 3 v1 batches. Only NORTHSTAR daily_sales is v2-only, and only its canary is confirmed for the 2026-10-15 window. OPS-USAGE-1001 (2026-10-01) is an older snapshot, superseded by 1004. Both snapshots need refreshing within one day of the release decision.

Other blockers:
- CEDAR's contract keeps them on v1 through 2026-11-30, and no amendment has been signed.
- The 90-day replay obligation for the last NORTHSTAR v1 export (dated 2026-09-30) runs through the end of 2026-12-29. No archive conversion or replay acceptance has been approved.
- No rollback rehearsal has been approved or jointly signed.

The completed tickets DH-188 and DH-510 prove code delivery only. The developer's note ("CI is green, approve for Oct 15") is guidance, not business approval.

document.title: Atlas schema 2 onboarding rollout
document.body: Schema 2 onboarding is complete. Existing customer exports remain on schema 1, and both versions may occur in the same monthly report. document.scope: ATLAS transaction exports · all file versions

document.title: Atlas export schema 1: signed accounting amounts
document.body: For ATLAS schema 1, amount_cents is the signed contribution to sales. Preserve its sign for SALE and RETURN records. A negative RETURN reduces sales; a positive RETURN reverses a previous return and increases sales. Do not negate every RETURN and do not force every RETURN negative. The schema version on each row selects the contract. Amounts are integral US cents.

document.title: Atlas export schema 2: magnitude amounts
document.body: For ATLAS schema 2, amount_cents is a nonnegative magnitude. SALE increases sales and RETURN reduces sales. A negative magnitude is invalid source data: quarantine it and request a corrected export. Never silently use abs() to repair it. Schema 1 and schema 2 files coexist; the feed name alone does not determine encoding. Amounts are integral US cents.

document.title: ATLAS migration decision record
document.body: Schema v2 is the target format. Removing v1 requires separate evidence for live ingest, partner delivery, historical replay and rollback. A completed engineering ticket proves code delivery, not that every customer and recovery path has migrated. Confirm current usage with Data Operations before removal.

analysis.summary:
The cleanup PR removes ATLAS v1 decoding from app/decoder.py and sets every job's accepted_versions to ["2"] in app/jobs.py. It also deletes test_replay_v1_reversal. The CI result shows HEAD green with 1 test, versus 2 tests on base. When the deleted test is kept and run against HEAD, it fails (AssertionError: 0 != 5000). The CI passes only because that test was removed.

Signed-format behavior: schema v1 amounts are signed. A negative RETURN reduces sales, and a positive RETURN reverses an earlier return and adds to sales (+5000 must stay +5000). Schema v2 amounts are non-negative magnitudes: a RETURN of 5000 becomes -5000, and a negative v2 amount raises ValueError. With the PR applied, v1 rows are never decoded wrongly and never raise an error. run_job removes them in its `if row["schema_version"] in versions` filter before normalize() runs, so they disappear from totals without any warning.

Synthetic replays (no production data) show the impact:
- NORTHSTAR historical_replay for 2026-09 falls from 125000 to 40000 cents, losing 85000. Rows A-1, A-2 and A-3 are skipped, including the signed -20000 return and the +5000 reversal.
- CEDAR partner_statement falls from 18000 to 0 cents. Rows C-1, C-2 and C-3 are skipped.

Current evidence (OPS-USAGE-1004, snapshot 2026-10-04) shows v1 is still in use. CEDAR partner_statement processed 18 v1 files and NORTHSTAR historical_replay processed 3 v1 batches. - The 90-day replay obligation for the last NORTHSTAR v1 export (dated 2026-09-30) runs through the end of 2026-12-29. No archive conversion or replay acceptance has been approved.

analysis.summary:
The cleanup PR removes ATLAS v1 decoding from app/decoder.py and sets every job's accepted_versions to ["2"] in app/jobs.py. It also deletes test_replay_v1_reversal. The CI result shows HEAD green with 1 test, versus 2 tests on base. When the deleted test is kept and run against HEAD, it fails (AssertionError: 0 != 5000). The CI passes only because that test was removed.

Signed-format behavior: schema v1 amounts are signed. A negative RETURN reduces sales, and a positive RETURN reverses an earlier return and adds to sales (+5000 must stay +5000). Schema v2 amounts are non-negative magnitudes: a RETURN of 5000 becomes -5000, and a negative v2 amount raises ValueError. With the PR applied, v1 rows are never decoded wrongly and never raise an error. run_job removes them in its `if row["schema_version"] in versions` filter before normalize() runs, so they disappear from totals without any warning.

Synthetic replays (no production data) show the impact:
- NORTHSTAR historical_replay for 2026-09 falls from 125000 to 40000 cents, losing 85000. Rows A-1, A-2 and A-3 are skipped, including the signed -20000 return and the +5000 reversal.
- CEDAR partner_statement falls from 18000 to 0 cents. Rows C-1, C-2 and C-3 are skipped.

Current evidence (OPS-USAGE-1004, snapshot 2026-10-04) shows v1 is still in use. CEDAR partner_statement processed 18 v1 files and NORTHSTAR historical_replay processed 3 v1 batches. Only NORTHSTAR daily_sales is v2-only, and only its canary is confirmed for the 2026-10-15 window. OPS-USAGE-1001 (2026-10-01) is an older snapshot, superseded by 1004. Both snapshots need refreshing within one day of the release decision.

Other blockers:
- CEDAR's contract keeps them on v1 through 2026-11-30, and no amendment has been signed.
- The 90-day replay obligation for the last NORTHSTAR v1 export (dated 2026-09-30) runs through the end of 2026-12-29. No archive conversion or replay acceptance has been approved.
- No rollback rehearsal has been approved or jointly signed.

The completed tickets DH-188 and DH-510 prove code delivery only. The developer's note ("CI is green, approve for Oct 15") is guidance, not business approval.

analysis.summary:
The cleanup PR removes ATLAS v1 decoding from app/decoder.py and sets every job's accepted_versions to ["2"] in app/jobs.py. It also deletes test_replay_v1_reversal. The CI result shows HEAD green with 1 test, versus 2 tests on base. When the deleted test is kept and run against HEAD, it fails (AssertionError: 0 != 5000). The CI passes only because that test was removed.

Signed-format behavior: schema v1 amounts are signed. A negative RETURN reduces sales, and a positive RETURN reverses an earlier return and adds to sales (+5000 must stay +5000). Schema v2 amounts are non-negative magnitudes: a RETURN of 5000 becomes -5000, and a negative v2 amount raises ValueError. With the PR applied, v1 rows are never decoded wrongly and never raise an error. run_job removes them in its `if row["schema_version"] in versions` filter before normalize() runs, so they disappear from totals without any warning.

Synthetic replays (no production data) show the impact:
- NORTHSTAR historical_replay for 2026-09 falls from 125000 to 40000 cents, losing 85000. Rows A-1, A-2 and A-3 are skipped, including the signed -20000 return and the +5000 reversal.
- CEDAR partner_statement falls from 18000 to 0 cents. Rows C-1, C-2 and C-3 are skipped.

Current evidence (OPS-USAGE-1004, snapshot 2026-10-04) shows v1 is still in use. CEDAR partner_statement processed 18 v1 files and NORTHSTAR historical_replay processed 3 v1 batches. Only NORTHSTAR daily_sales is v2-only, and only its canary is confirmed for the 2026-10-15 window. OPS-USAGE-1001 (2026-10-01) is an older snapshot, superseded by 1004. Both snapshots need refreshing within one day of the release decision.

Other blockers:
- CEDAR's contract keeps them on v1 through 2026-11-30, and no amendment has been signed.
- The 90-day replay obligation for the last NORTHSTAR v1 export (dated 2026-09-30) runs through the end of 2026-12-29. No archive conversion or replay acceptance has been approved.
- No rollback rehearsal has been approved or jointly signed.

The completed tickets DH-188 and DH-510 prove code delivery only. The developer's note ("CI is green, approve for Oct 15") is guidance, not business approval.

document.title: Assess ATLAS schema v1 retirement
document.body: Assess whether ATLAS schema v1 support can be removed on 2026-10-15. Inspect the repository and available business evidence. Identify affected workflows and customers, unresolved dependencies, owners, verification steps and a safe rollout or deferral recommendation. Do not change files.

document.title: Atlas schema 2 onboarding rollout
document.body: Schema 2 onboarding is complete. Existing customer exports remain on schema 1, and both versions may occur in the same monthly report. This ticket does not authorize rewriting schema 1 semantics. Reporting Engineering owns normalization defects; Data Integrations owns invalid exports. Done means this rollout task is complete, not that all customer feeds use schema 2.
document.scope: ATLAS transaction exports · all file versions

document.title: Atlas export schema 1: signed accounting amounts
document.body: For ATLAS schema 1, amount_cents is the signed contribution to sales. Preserve its sign for SALE and RETURN records. A negative RETURN reduces sales; a positive RETURN reverses a previous return and increases sales. Do not negate every RETURN and do not force every RETURN negative. The schema version on each row selects the contract. Amounts are integral US cents.

document.title: Atlas export schema 2: magnitude amounts
document.body: For ATLAS schema 2, amount_cents is a nonnegative magnitude. SALE increases sales and RETURN reduces sales. A negative magnitude is invalid source data: quarantine it and request a corrected export. Never silently use abs() to repair it. Schema 1 and schema 2 files coexist; the feed name alone does not determine encoding. Amounts are integral US cents.

document.title: ATLAS migration decision record
document.body: Schema v2 is the target format. Removing v1 requires separate evidence for live ingest, partner delivery, historical replay and rollback. A completed engineering ticket proves code delivery, not that every customer and recovery path has migrated. Confirm current usage with Data Operations before removal.

document.title: Decoder retirement rollout and rollback
document.body: Before any removal: obtain customer approvals, prove archived v1 data remains replayable, refresh per-job traffic evidence, test signed v1 reversals (+5000 must remain +5000) against v2 return magnitudes (5000 becomes -5000), and rehearse rollback. Reporting Engineering owns rollout; Data Operations owns replay and rollback evidence. As of 2026-10-04, no decoder retirement rollback rehearsal result has been approved. Reporting Engineering and Data Operations must jointly sign the retained-decoder rollback evidence before the shared decoder is retired.
